category.title: 训练结束时在响应什么（AI 归类）
category.title_en: What it responds to by the end of training (AI-sorted)

cluster.title: 变化曲线相似的神经元（自动分组）
cluster.title_en: Neurons whose curves changed alike (automatic groups)

0.name: 底层迟发定型
0.desc: 几乎集中在0层；前中期多次更替，选择性到中期已高，但词元与文档直到末段才对齐并稳定。激活尖锐度后期反而下降。
0.desc_en: Concentrated almost entirely in layer 0; undergoes multiple changes in the early and middle stages. Selectivity is already high by mid-training, but tokens and documents do not align and stabilize until the final stage. Activation sharpness declines in the later stages.

1.name: 渐尖锐收敛
1.desc: 层位分散；中后期选择性快速升高，激活持续变尖锐，词元与文档逐步对齐，但末期稳定性仍不及早定型簇。
1.desc_en: Distributed across layers; selectivity rises rapidly in the middle-to-late stages, and activations continuously sharpen. Tokens and documents gradually align, but stability at the end remains lower than in the early-stabilization cluster.

2.name: 广层缓慢成形
2.desc: 覆盖几乎所有层；选择性稳步升至最高，尖锐度仅小幅增加。后期仍有漂移，文档对齐尤其滞后，成员多见异质模式混合。
2.desc_en: Spans almost all layers; selectivity steadily rises to the highest level, while sharpness increases only slightly. Drift persists in the later stages, with document alignment especially delayed. Members often exhibit mixtures of heterogeneous patterns.

3.name: 中层锐化转型
3.desc: 偏中高层；早期粗粒度相关性虽高却回落，之后选择性迅速拉满、激活明显变尖锐。中后期才逐步定型，常见主题替换后局部扩展。
3.desc_en: Skews toward middle and upper layers; early coarse-grained correlations are high but decline, followed by a rapid rise in selectivity to its maximum and pronounced activation sharpening. Stabilization occurs only gradually in the middle-to-late stages; topic replacement followed by local expansion is common.

4.name: 高层钝化游移
4.desc: 集中高层；尖锐度基本不变且选择性始终偏低，文档稳定度最低，训练末期仍较游移，成员常保留多种难归并模式。
4.name_en: Blunting and wandering in upper layers
4.desc_en: Concentrated in upper layers; sharpness remains largely unchanged and selectivity stays low throughout. Document stability is the lowest, and patterns remain relatively unsettled even at the end of training. Members often retain multiple patterns that are difficult to consolidate.

5.name: 高层混合渐锐
5.desc: 集中高层；初始选择性异常高后骤降，随后缓慢回升；激活逐渐变尖锐但仍不算集中，后期虽收敛，异质模式与跨域混合突出。
5.desc_en: Concentrated in upper layers; initially anomalously high selectivity drops sharply, then slowly recovers. Activations gradually sharpen but remain diffuse. Although they converge in the later stages, heterogeneous patterns and cross-domain mixtures are prominent.

recursive_generalization.name: 从核心延伸（递归泛化）
recursive_generalization.desc: 先有一个核心内容，之后逐渐延伸到相关的内容
recursive_generalization.name_en: Grew out from a core (recursive generalization)
recursive_generalization.desc_en: Starts from one core idea and later extends to related ideas

superposition.name: 无关内容并存（superposition）
superposition.desc: 同时响应几种毫不相干的内容，找不到共同的核心
superposition.desc_en: Holds several unrelated things at once, with no shared core

replacement.name: 整体换成别的内容
replacement.desc: 早期的内容被丢掉，换成了一个不相关的新内容
replacement.desc_en: An early idea is dropped and an unrelated one takes its place

stable_monosemantic.name: 始终是同一种内容
stable_monosemantic.desc: 从某个阶段起，一直只响应同一种内容
stable_monosemantic.desc_en: From some point on, it responds to one single thing

mixed.name: 混合
mixed.desc: 以上几种情况同时存在
mixed.desc_en: Shows several of these at once

uninterpretable.name: 看不出规律
uninterpretable.desc: 大多数阶段 AI 都没找到规律
uninterpretable.desc_en: At most stages the AI could not find a pattern

diff.title: 是否像去噪一样逐步变清晰（AI 判断）
diff.title_en: Did it sharpen gradually, like denoising? (AI judgment)

denoising.name: 逐步变清晰（像去噪）
denoising.desc: 一步步定型，先定大方向再定细节，越来越清晰
denoising.desc_en: Settled step by step, broad direction first, getting clearer over time

drift.name: 中途换了内容
drift.desc: 中途换成别的内容，之后才稳定下来
drift.desc_en: Switched to different content before settling

phase_transition.name: 突然出现
phase_transition.desc: 最终内容是一下子出现的
phase_transition.desc_en: Its final idea showed up all at once

early_fixed.name: 很早就定型
early_fixed.desc: 很早就成形，之后几乎不变
early_fixed.desc_en: Took its final form early and barely changed after

late_degradation.name: 后期变模糊
late_degradation.desc: 训练后期反而变得不清晰
late_degradation.desc_en: Became less clear late in training

dominant.title: 训练后期的强反应主要来自哪种演化机制
dominant.title_en: Which evolution mechanism its strongest late-training responses mostly come from

branch.name: 主要来自分支（递归泛化）
branch.desc: 训练后期最强的反应里，一半以上来自从已有概念长出的概念
branch.desc_en: More than half of its strongest late responses come from concepts that grew out of an earlier concept

coexist.name: 主要来自无关共存
coexist.desc: 一半以上来自出现时与已有概念无关、并与它们并存的概念（可能是 superposition）
coexist.desc_en: More than half come from concepts that arose unrelated to the existing ones and coexist with them (possibly superposition)

replace.name: 主要来自替换
replace.desc: 一半以上来自接替了某个死去概念的概念
replace.desc_en: More than half come from concepts that took the place of a concept that died

sporadic.name: 主要是零散特征
sporadic.desc: 一半以上来自只在一个阶段出现过的概念
sporadic.desc_en: More than half come from concepts that appear at only one stage

none.name: 没有明显主体
none.desc: 没有哪种机制超过一半
none.desc_en: No mechanism accounts for more than half

neurons.label: Australian
neurons.core: 后期稳定模式为 Australian 字符串/澳大利亚相关修饰语；早期核心并未延续
neurons.rg_summary: 神经元先后响应多个互不相关的字符串或专名，直到训练后期才稳定转为 Australian 模式；整体最符合 replacement，而非沿核心扩展的递归泛化。
neurons.rg_evidence: 定量重合度显示前期状态与最终 Australian 模式不连续：step 0–96000 的 tok 均为 0，doc 至多 0.08；step 128000 才跃至 1。NH、Twitter 与后续地名/字符串模式也未显示可追溯的共同分支，因此更像多次无关替换，而非递归泛化。
unrelated: NH 字符串（step 0–512）
Twitter 提及（step 1000–2000）
一系列彼此不同的字符串或地名：dong、Seoul、Amsterdam、ENG、Brisbane、London、Wellington、Shanghai（step 4000–96000）
neurons.diff_summary: 该神经元经历了多次概念漂移，直到 step 128000 才呈现最终的 Australian 词特征，不符合扩散式渐进去噪。
neurons.diff_evidence: 早期特征明确是 NH 字符串（step 0–512），step 1000 转为 Twitter，随后 step 4000–96000 多次变为不同字符串或地名，且 det 多次降至 0.50。最终 Australian 概念到 step 128000 才出现；此前 tok 为 0，说明这是明显漂移，而非渐进去噪。clarity 与 det 波动，尽管后期 clarity 较高。

en.label: Australian
en.core: The final stable pattern is the Australian string and Australia-related modifiers; the early core did not persist
en.rg_summary: The neuron responded to several unrelated strings or proper nouns in succession, only stabilizing into an Australian pattern late in training. Overall, this is most consistent with replacement rather than recursive generalization extending from a core.
en.rg_evidence: Quantitative overlap shows that the earlier states were discontinuous with the final Australian pattern: tok was 0 for steps 0–96000, and doc was at most 0.08; only at step 128000 did it jump to 1. The NH, Twitter, and later place-name/string patterns also show no traceable shared branch, making this more like multiple unrelated replacements than recursive generalization.
en.diff_summary: The neuron underwent multiple instances of concept drift and did not exhibit the final Australian lexical feature until step 128000, inconsistent with gradual denoising through diffusion.
en.diff_evidence: The early feature was clearly the NH string (steps 0–512), which shifted to Twitter at step 1000, then changed multiple times to different strings or place names during steps 4000–96000; det also fell to 0.50 multiple times. The final Australian concept appeared only at step 128000; tok was 0 before then, indicating clear drift rather than gradual denoising. Clarity and det fluctuated, although clarity was higher later.
en.core_summary: Australia-related regional, national, and institutional attributes, with Australian as the core trigger word.

neurons.label: Pl 字符片段
neurons.core: 大写词首或词内的字符片段“Pl”
neurons.rg_summary: 神经元早期经历多个互不相关的模式，训练中后期收敛并稳定为检测“Pl”字符片段。
neurons.rg_evidence: 最终模式是跨词汇、语言和领域稳定出现的 Pl 字符片段；step 32000 起 tok、doc 均为 1，且后续持续一致。早期 weaken、数字、execut、amel 与最终模式无关，说明发生过概念替换，而非这些模式沿共同核心分支生长。step 4000 起的 pl 与最终 Pl 有正字形连续性，但数据更支持后期稳定重定向，不能证明递归分支链。

step 4000–24000：pl 字符串检测（与最终 Pl 正字形模式相近，但不完全相同）
neurons.diff_summary: 该神经元经历多次概念漂移，约在 32000 才定为最终的 Pl 字符片段检测器，不符合扩散式逐步收敛。
neurons.diff_evidence: step 0–128 的概念是 weaken，256–512 转为数字串，1000–24000 又先后落在 execut、amel、pl/PL 等不同模式；这些阶段 tok、doc 均接近 0。最终 Pl 词首模式在 32000 才出现，此时 tok、doc 突然为 1，非渐进去噪。清晰度也在 256 明显下降，后期基本较高但有波动。

en.label: Pl character fragment
en.core: The character fragment “Pl” at the start or within words, in uppercase
en.rg_summary: The neuron initially exhibits several unrelated patterns, then converges and stabilizes late in training as a detector for the “Pl” character fragment.
en.rg_evidence: The final pattern is a Pl character fragment that appears consistently across vocabularies, languages, and domains; tok and doc are both 1 from step 32000 onward and remain consistent thereafter. The early weaken, number, execut, and amel patterns are unrelated to the final pattern, indicating conceptual replacement rather than growth of these patterns along a shared core branch. pl from step 4000 has positive orthographic continuity with the final Pl pattern, but the data better supports late stable redirection and does not prove a recursive branch chain.
en.diff_summary: This neuron undergoes multiple instances of conceptual drift and settles as a detector for the final Pl character fragment only around step 32000, inconsistent with gradual, diffusion-like convergence.
en.diff_evidence: The concept is weaken at steps 0–128, shifts to number strings at 256–512, and then successively exhibits execut, amel, and pl/PL patterns from 1000–24000; tok and doc are both close to 0 during these stages. The final Pl word-initial pattern appears only at 32000, when tok and doc suddenly become 1, indicating non-gradual denoising. Clarity also drops markedly at 256 and is generally high later, with some fluctuation.
en.core_summary: The Pl character fragment, especially at the start of words or across tokens in the form Pl; in later stages it consistently covers semantically diverse word forms.

steps 256–512: number strings and structured-text cues

en.label: Far character fragment
en.core: The final stable core is the word-initial substring “Far,” primarily triggered by orthography rather than a unified semantic concept; other word-form cores appeared briefly in the middle of training.
en.rg_summary: The neuron underwent multiple early replacements by unrelated word forms, then converged to a stable Far string detector. Its evolution therefore combines replacement with a single stable pattern in the later stages.
en.rg_evidence: The early core changed repeatedly among Building, blessing, RM, and others, and coarse-grained preferences also fluctuated. far appeared starting at step 8000; from step 16000 onward, tok/doc overlap with the final checkpoint rapidly reached 0.95/0.91, then stabilized on the Far string. Later polysemy mostly involves the same subword fragment and is insufficient to establish a semantic branch; early change coexists with later stability.
en.diff_summary: The neuron underwent clear mid-training concept drift, shifting around step 16000 to the final Far string feature rather than gradually denoising toward convergence from an early pattern.
en.diff_evidence: Early interpretations repeatedly shifted among patterns involving Building, blessing, RM, Lemma/communicated, undefined, stranded, tables, and far. At step 16000, tok=0.95 and doc=0.91, marking the first strong overlap with the final Far string pattern; at step 32000, they fully overlapped. Clarity and detection score fluctuated repeatedly, inconsistent with smooth denoising.
en.core_summary: The word-initial Far string fragment, which in later stages mainly activates in Faraday and Faraday rotation contexts; it also generalizes to other names and words beginning with Far.

en.label: Same or equivalent
en.core: Represents the semantic feature of sameness or equivalence (primarily carried by identical, later expanding to same)
en.rg_summary: The neuron’s early patterns changed several times, then stably encoded the concept of sameness expressed by identical for an extended period. Near the end, it briefly shifted to the synonym same before returning.
en.rg_evidence: Early patterns changed substantially across checkpoints, with almost no overlap with the final state. Starting at step 8000, identical had tok and doc scores of 1, remaining stable through step 96000; at step 128000, it changed to same, with tok/doc dropping to 0.11/0.08, then finally returned to identical. Since same is semantically related to identical, this is more consistent with replacement by a related concept than with unrelated superposition.
en.diff_summary: After several instances of concept drift, the neuron stabilized on the concept of sameness around step 8000, which is inconsistent with gradual denoising evolution.
en.diff_evidence: Early patterns were chaotic and did not overlap with the final concept; Dutch articles and sinus appeared sequentially at steps 2000–6000, indicating an intermediate concept change. Starting at step 8000, identical appeared, with clarity and det reaching high levels and remaining stable. tok/doc were both 1 at this point, but at step 128000 it briefly shifted to same, showing a change in fine-grained samples late in training.
en.core_summary: The sameness or equivalence relation expressed by identical; later, it stably carries the concept that compared objects, results, conditions, or properties are the same.

en.label: about/around usage
en.core: Detection of common English word forms, ultimately stabilizing on prepositional and adverbial uses such as around/about; there is no evidence that early Fermi, Caf, loyalty, opportunity, or MOT are its semantic core
en.rg_summary: This neuron initially passes through several unrelated terms, then stabilizes as a detector for the polysemous word form around, and shifts to about at the end. It therefore appears to reflect a mixed evolution involving recursive semantic branches and concept replacement.
en.rg_evidence: Starting at step 6000, coarse rises from 0.83 to 0.98 at 32000, then approaches 1, supporting gradual stabilization of the around pattern; however, tok does not reach 1 until 96000, and the final about differs from around at step 128000, suggesting late-stage replacement. The early unrelated terms do not persist; steps 0–128 should not be treated as core.
en.diff_summary: The neuron undergoes multiple concept changes, with further variation between around and about later on. This best fits drift, rather than gradual convergence from noise to a single concept.
en.diff_evidence: The activation concepts change markedly: early Fermi (step 0–256), followed by Caf, loyalty, opportunity, and MOT, then shifting to Around/around from step 6000. The interpretation at step 96000 changes to about, and the final checkpoint is also about; step 128000, however, returns to around. Quantitative overlap shows almost no overlap between the early and final tokens; fine-grained overlap appears only at step 96000. No gradual denoising toward a stable single concept is evident.
en.core_summary: Spatial, range-related, and other polysemous uses of around appear consistently later on; about also appears at the end with approximate and topic-introducing uses, but does not constitute the same core concept.
unrelated: The Fermi physics-term pattern at steps 0–128 has almost no quantitative overlap with the final checkpoint and belongs to the random-initialization phase, so it is not core evidence

en.label: Dou spelling fragment
en.core: No stable semantic core; the stable feature formed in late training is the Dou spelling fragment
en.rg_summary: Early and mid-training, this neuron was repeatedly triggered by unrelated word forms or character fragments, stabilizing on the Dou substring only at the end. This primarily reflects replacement rather than recursive generalization.
en.rg_evidence: Quantitative overlap shows that concepts were continually replaced mid-training: tok was 0 at steps 0–64000, with doc around 0.00–0.02; only at step 96000 was the state highly similar to the final state (coarse=.94, tok=.95). However, at step 128000, tok=.38 and doc=.23, indicating that the final Dou pattern was established only at the end. The change in wording is supported by the overlap scores and does not resemble branches growing from a shared core.
en.diff_summary: This neuron switched repeatedly among different character or stem patterns during training, forming a Dou spelling-fragment detector only later. This is more consistent with drift than with gradual, diffusion-like denoising.
en.diff_evidence: Early patterns changed across checkpoints: Ik, rives, τ, discrimin/propag, recogn, Give, Cyrillic fragments, and others. Their tok and doc overlap with the final state was essentially zero, indicating mid-training drift rather than gradual convergence. Although tok=0.95 at step 96000, the pattern was still primarily the ou fragment; it was not identified as Dou until step 128000, when doc was still only 0.23. det and clarity fluctuated substantially; final clarity=3, with no evidence of monotonic denoising or clear saturation.

en.label: Source-code comment terminator */
en.core: Source-code comment terminator « */»
en.rg_summary: The neuron passes through multiple mid-stage patterns with no apparent connection, then stabilizes on the source-code comment terminator, showing a mixture of superposition and later replacement.
en.rg_evidence: Mid-stage patterns change repeatedly, focusing on anecdotal, Of, and none, with no visible branch relationships. The final checkpoint stabilizes on « */», with a quantitative overlap of 1 with step 128000. The available metrics cannot establish that these mid-stage patterns recursively grew from a shared core.
en.diff_summary: The evolution shows clear conceptual drift: the final source-code comment terminator is not identifiable until 128000, rather than gradually converging through denoising from earlier patterns.
en.diff_evidence: The early pattern is mainly Mock. Between 1000 and 96000, interpretations shift in turn to repay, multilingual fragments, sentence-initial Of, anecdotal, none, and others, with extremely low overlap with the final state. The final concept, the source-code comment terminator, first appears at 128000, when tok/doc suddenly rises to 1. Clarity and SNR fluctuate repeatedly rather than showing gradual, monotonic denoising.

en.label: paying
en.core: paying word form (payment-related usage)
en.rg_summary: The neuron successively exhibits multiple unrelated word forms or code patterns, stabilizing on paying in the final stages; there is no indication that branches recursively grew from a single core.
en.rg_evidence: Quantitative overlap shows repeated changes between checkpoints: step 6000 and final tok/doc are .92/.86, but step 8000 is 1/1; overlap then drops to near zero at steps 12000–64000 and recovers to 1/1 from step 96000 onward. Paying is stable in later stages, but there is no evidence that travers, word families, brackets, or NULL branch from it; overall, this looks more like repeated replacement by unrelated patterns, interspersed with brief co-occurrence.
en.diff_summary: The evolution involves multiple instances of conceptual drift, ultimately returning to and stabilizing on paying at step 96000, rather than gradually denoising and converging from noise.
en.diff_evidence: Early on, the pattern is litre; at steps 512–4000, different forms such as travers, intellig, and Treasure also appear. At step 6000, the neuron is interpreted as encoding two groups of unrelated patterns; only at step 8000 does it stabilize on paying. It then shifts to structural symbols, NULL, and other concepts at steps 12000–64000, before stabilizing on paying again at step 96000. Clarity metrics are also non-monotonic; although they are high in later stages, snr declines.

en.label: signed/sign
en.core: Sign or join (signed/sign, a stable late-stage form and functional pattern)
en.rg_summary: The neuron showed multiple unrelated patterns in the early and middle stages, then converged on a stable signed/sign feature for signing, extending to a related registration use.
en.rg_evidence: Early features varied and were unrelated, with no persistent core. From step 64000, tok/doc had reached .98/.97 similarity to the final state; after step 96000, they fully overlapped. The final signed/sign semantics are stable and include a related signed up branch; unrelated co-resident patterns are also prominent in the early and middle stages.
en.diff_summary: The neuron underwent several conceptual drifts and settled on its final signing/registration feature only around step 64000, rather than gradually denoising from an ambiguous early state.
en.diff_evidence: Early features were mainly distinct subword fragments, including oli, \alpha, VAL, and Nguyen; different patterns continued to recur from step 2000–48000. The final “signing/registration” concept became clearly apparent only at step 64000, when tok/doc were already close to the final state; it remained stable thereafter. det, clarity, and snr also fluctuated markedly, inconsistent with gradual, monotonic denoising.

en.label: put string
en.core: letter string put
en.rg_summary: Early on, multiple unrelated word-form patterns were replaced; later, a stable cross-lingual string detector centered on put emerged, combining superposition-like switching with local recursive generalization.
en.rg_evidence: The final state is dominated by the put string; from step 64000 onward, tok and doc are both 1. Explanations show that forms within English and cross-lingual words share the same string, supporting a branch that generalizes from put to the string. However, the earlier patterns underwent multiple unrelated switches, and put did not continue from the early core, so both types of evolution are clearly present.
en.diff_summary: The neuron underwent multiple instances of concept drift, ultimately stabilizing around step 64000 as a put string feature. This does not fit a diffusion-like, gradual denoising trajectory.
en.diff_evidence: Early patterns involved beginnings/portrayed and other forms, followed in turn by witnessing, spread/trapped, transplanted, and put; the neuron ultimately stabilized on the letter string put. The final concept did not gradually converge from the early patterns, but changed multiple times along the way; only at step 64000 did it fully match the final token and document. Multiple high det/clarity scores do not imply conceptual continuity; scores were already high early on, and overall clarity was not monotonic.
en.core_summary: The continuous letter string put in English and cross-lingual word forms; later, the neuron stably detects this string without requiring an independent verb usage.
unrelated: Patterns from step 0–16000, including beginnings, portrayed, furnish, create, witnessing, trapped, republished, screwed, plung, ún, Unlock, and transplanted, are unrelated to the later put pattern; multiple unrelated word-form pattern switches occurred among them

en.diff_summary: The neuron passes through several distinct concepts mid-training, shifting to the final tele-substring feature at around step 6000 and then stabilizing, consistent with drift rather than diffusion-like denoising.
en.diff_evidence: The final recognizable tele-string concept appears around step 6000, with tok/doc both at 1 from step 12000 onward. en.label: str string

Starting at step 48000, coarse-grained overlap with the final state rises to 0.92, with tok/doc at 0.52/0.36; after step 64000, overlap stabilizes at 1, and the interpretation gradually converges on the character fragment str.
en.diff_summary: The neuron undergoes multiple instances of concept drift and finally stabilizes around step 64000 on the character substring “str,” rather than gradually denoising from an early concept.
en.diff_evidence: Early patterns involve mathematical/scientific text. en.core_summary: The late-stage stable core is the contiguous character substring str, independent of specific meanings or context.

en.label: Academic citations and formatting markers
en.core: Citation and cross-reference markers in scientific documents
en.rg_summary: The neuron responds to multiple unrelated terms in succession. Around step 4000, an academic-document marker lineage emerges, while numerous sporadic terminology fragments persist later, indicating mixed evolution.
en.rg_evidence: Early terms change repeatedly and have little overlap with later ones. Starting at step 4000, citation markers become the dominant pattern; tok rises to 0.59–1 at steps 6000–8000, and later figure and table citation markers are structurally associated with them. Later, tok/coarse approach 1, but doc remains low and samples consist mainly of terminology fragments. This suggests both unrelated replacement and the coexistence of a structural-marker lineage with later scattered terms.
en.diff_summary: The neuron undergoes early conceptual drift, shifting around step 4000 toward features related to academic-document markers. Overlap then increases, but clarity declines overall, and the coarse-to-fine ordering does not hold.
en.diff_evidence: Early identifications progress through malignancies, Denis, Acad, Frequency, and mic, showing substantial conceptual drift. After step 4000, the neuron shifts toward academic citations/document structure, and coarse and tok gradually approach the final state, but fine-grained doc reaches only 0.47 by step 128000. Clarity falls from 5 to 2–3, with no sustained increase in clarity later.
en.core_summary: The stable later core concept is citation markers in scientific text, especially citation boundaries formed by square brackets/parentheses and @.

en.label: Title format beginning with a year
en.core: A format marker at the beginning of a text fragment or entry, later stabilizing specifically as a year-first title/record
en.rg_summary: The neuron initially cycles through several unrelated patterns, then develops and stabilizes into a year-first title format, with clear replacement and later recursive expansion.
en.rg_evidence: The early Med, pen, Steve, and Currently patterns are unrelated in content to the later year-first titles, with zero or very low tok/doc overlap, indicating early pattern replacement. Year/title signals appear around step 12000; after step 48000, the pattern becomes more coherent, coarse rises from 0.98 to 1, and tok/doc remain close to the final state.
en.diff_summary: Overall, the evidence supports a denoising-like evolution that first forms a coarse preference for title openings and then gradually approaches specific end-state contexts, though mid-stage fluctuations make the evidence inconclusive.
en.diff_evidence: Early features are mixed and have low overlap with the final state; terms change frequently from step 4000–32000, but the coarse preference remains close to the final state. From step 48000, the year/title pattern is clear, and tok/doc continue to rise afterward, with no evident intermediate replacement concept that stabilizes. clarity, det, and snr fluctuate, and do not increase strictly monotonically in the later stages.

en.label: Term-internal subword fragments
en.core: Term-fragment triggers in academic and technical text (later more consistently biased toward statistical-function vocabulary such as distribution/function, but without a single semantic core sustained throughout)
en.rg_summary: The neuron passes through multiple non-continuous patterns in succession. Later it favors academic terminology but remains mixed; overall, this resembles a hybrid evolution involving conceptual replacement and unrelated patterns co-residing.
en.rg_evidence: Early on, AS, GSH, and “We have” appear in succession without continuing. From the middle to later stages, coarse-grained preferences gradually approach the final state (rising from step 4000), but fine-grained token overlap does not increase substantially until step 48000, reaching 0.92 at step 96000. The final stage still mixes nov, os, and function terms, supporting some clustering of academic terminology but not enough to establish branch-like recursive growth.
en.diff_summary: Overall, this shows prolonged cross-concept drift and instability in the final stage, rather than diffusion-style denoising evolution supported by sufficient evidence.
en.diff_evidence: Early AS/GSH and “We have” at step 1000 both differ from the final sporadic term fragments. Final token overlap reaches 1 only at step 128000, and document overlap was also low before then. Function terms at step 96000 may be viewed as a temporarily discernible pattern, but subsequently become unclear again. Clarity fluctuates repeatedly, with no gradual and stable denoising convergence.
en.core_summary: Function, distribution, and model terminology in academic and technical text; later consistently covers probability density functions and related functions, as well as scientific-paper prose and machine-learning models.
unrelated: Capitalized AS string patterns at step 0–128, which do not continue afterward

The “We have” research-progress sentence structure at step 1000, with no clear connection to later subword-fragment patterns
The relationships among sporadic word forms and derivative patterns at step 2000–8000, and between these and later patterns, are unclear
nov/supernova and os subword fragments at step 128000–143000, co-residing with patterns such as function and lacking a shared semantic core

en.label: Scientific and technical text format
en.core: Formatting and structural markers in dates and academic/scientific texts (later stably biased toward scientific and technical text fragments)
en.rg_summary: The neuron’s early string triggers did not persist. By mid-training, it shifted to date and document-format patterns, then stabilized on scientific and technical text formatting, with clear replacement and some thematic refinement.
en.rg_evidence: The Debbie/she pattern has zero tok and doc overlap with the mid- and late-training patterns, indicating that the concept did not persist. The date pattern emerges around step 4000, followed by a shift toward academic structure and scientific formatting; coarse/tok are closer to the final state in later stages, while doc increases only late in training. There are both unrelated early patterns and gradual refinement of the formatting theme, which fits mixed evolution better than a single recursive branch.
en.diff_summary: The neuron underwent clear mid-training concept drift, then gradually converged on academic and scientific text-format fragments, rather than evolving through continuous, diffusion-like denoising.
en.diff_evidence: Early patterns shift from she and subword fragments to paragraphs, War, and dates. From step 4000–12000, the date pattern is stable, after which it shifts toward paper structure and scientific formatting. Final similarity rises from step 32000 (tok 0.55, doc 0.19) and is higher later, but convergence is not smooth from the start. det/clarity fluctuate substantially several times, which does not support monotonic denoising.
en.core_summary: Crystallographic experimental parameters and scientific notation formatting: stable late-stage activation on Å, Kα, μ, mm⁻¹, and adjacent numerical parameter records.
unrelated: Debbie/she string triggers at step 0–128, with no quantitative overlap persisting into the stable post-training pattern

Sporadic intra-word fragment pattern at step 256, with low detectability and no reliable core

en.label: Multilingual intraword fragments
en.core: Responses to intraword letter/subword fragments in multilingual text
en.rg_summary: The neuron undergoes several successive changes in surface-form patterns, eventually tending toward multilingual intraword-fragment detection. There is some local continuity, alongside clear unrelated patterns, which is most consistent with mixed evolution.
en.rg_evidence: Early patterns change substantially across checkpoints and cannot be considered a stable core. Later, tok/doc and the final state gradually increase, while the o in emoji and intraword fragments continue to appear, indicating local continuity. However, the multilingual fragments and early triggers lack shared semantics or a clear branch lineage, so evidence for recursive generalization is limited, with unrelated patterns also present.
en.diff_summary: The trajectory looks more like drift among multiple early surface-form patterns, with a multilingual intraword-fragment feature emerging only at the end, rather than convergence through gradual denoising from an ambiguous state.
en.diff_evidence: Early patterns are dominated by beauty, HM, 1956, and sporadic letter fragments; step 1000–8000 also shows different surface-form triggers such as mult, Ge, and coordinate, and trigger patterns continue to change at step 12000–24000. The final multilingual intraword-fragment feature only gradually emerges later: tok rises from 0.05 at step 16000 to 0.83 at 128000, while doc rises from 0.11 to 0.52. det and clarity fluctuate repeatedly, with final clarity=2; this does not fit a stable, monotonic denoising process.
en.core_summary: In later stages, the neuron consistently responds to specific spelling fragments, mainly the letter o in the word emoji; the intraword fragment in the Portuguese word experiência also appears over an extended period. No single stable main concept is evident, so no core is assigned.
unrelated: Randomly initialized surface-form patterns at step 0–512, including beauty, involved, HM, Pres, onic, and Ish
Disjoint triggers at step 1000–12000, including mult-, Ge, coordinate, Importance/threshold, and touch

en.label: U.S. legal texts
en.core: Legal citations, litigation terminology, and formal names in U.S. legal texts
en.rg_summary: After early random word-form patterns faded, the neuron formed and gradually stabilized around features of U.S. legal texts, while retaining a few unrelated local triggers. Overall, it shows recursive expansion of a legal core, with mild superposition.
en.rg_evidence: Early patterns such as boast and Ne did not persist; after step 1000, the theme shifted to legal texts. Coarse-grained similarity rose to about 0.8 starting at step 2000 and approached the final state after step 4000; tok did not approach it clearly until step 24000, while doc remained low. The legal register expanded steadily, interspersed with several isolated character-form triggers.
en.diff_summary: Midway through, the neuron shifted from sporadic word-form triggers to features of legal texts. The coarse-grained legal register stabilized before specific tokens and contexts, which is more consistent with drift than with ongoing denoising evolution.
en.diff_evidence: Early patterns mainly involved the subword fragments boast, Ne, and Appellees; Convention appeared briefly at step 1000; steps 2000–6000 shifted to state names and constitutional-rights contexts; steps 8000–16000 featured proper nouns and legal vocabulary again. Only after step 24000 did it stabilize around U.S. legal texts, with tok/doc overlap with the final state increasing gradually. The concept changed substantially rather than monotonically denoising from an early fuzzy pattern to the final concept; clarity also fluctuated considerably.
en.core_summary: The later stable core consists of statutes, case citations, and their formatting in U.S. legal documents, along with related patterns involving legal procedure, jurisdictions, and institutional proper names.

en.label: Mixed subword fragments
en.core: Statistical and epidemiological reporting in medical research, especially expressions such as OR, risk, and prevalence
en.rg_summary: The neuron passed through multiple unstable patterns before forming a core branch in medical statistics and epidemiology, but later accumulated morphological activations that are difficult to explain through that core. Overall, this is a mixed evolution in which recursive generalization and superposition coexist.
en.rg_evidence: Early patterns had little overlap with the final state before step 6000. The medical statistics theme appeared around step 12000, with coarse-grained overlap rising to 0.73 and reaching 0.92 at step 32000, then remaining high. However, later token/doc overlap was still limited, and after 96000 the explanations consisted mainly of cross-lingual subword fragments, indicating that core semantics coexisted with unrelated morphological activations.
en.diff_summary: The activation underwent multiple conceptual drifts. Although its overlap with the final sample increased toward the end, it converged to an ambiguous mixture of subword fragments rather than a progressively clearer unified concept.
en.diff_evidence: Early activation patterns involving researchers, couple, chairman, and double hyphens appeared in succession. Only during step 6000–32000 did the pattern gradually focus on medical statistics, but high overlap did not yield stable clarity. After step 96000, tok/doc approached the final sample, yet consisted mainly of cross-lingual subword fragments. The final det=0.50 and clarity=2 do not reveal a unified concept. The metrics do not support sustained denoising toward a clear, stable end state.
en.core_summary: Reporting statistical associations and effect sizes in medical research, centered especially on OR, risk comparisons, and confidence intervals; later generalizing to medical research outcome reporting.

en.label: Formal mathematical terminology
en.core: Structural terminology and formal discourse in technical mathematical texts
en.rg_summary: The neuron exhibited sporadic patterns that did not persist early on, then stably converged on the core of formal mathematical texts, covering multiple mathematical branches within it.
en.rg_evidence: Early notes, -oplasmic, and noisy patterns did not persist; starting at step 16000, the neuron shifted to formal mathematical text, reaching tok/doc values of 0.80/0.73 at the final checkpoint (step 96000). It continued to approach the final state, consistent with generalization within the mathematical core. However, several early patterns were unrelated to one another and lacked evidence of lineage to the mathematical core, so the classification is mixed.
en.diff_summary: The neuron underwent several early instances of conceptual drift, stabilizing on formal mathematical text at around step 16000; thereafter, coarse-grained preferences converged before details.
en.diff_evidence: The early notes/footnote pattern persisted through step 256; at step 512 it shifted to biomedical fragments, and at steps 1000–2000, different patterns such as noisy and interesting appeared. From steps 4000–12000, it gradually shifted toward mathematical text, settling into a formal mathematical context after step 16000. Quantitative overlap also supports mid-course drift: tok was only 0.23 at step 12000, then rose steadily; clarity and det fluctuated multiple times, indicating non-monotonic denoising.
en.core_summary: Formal structural statements in mathematical papers: the later, stable response cluster concerns mathematical objects such as groups, rings, algebra, and homology, as well as their definitions, relations, and formulaic expressions.

en.label: word-final -ors
en.core: The English word ending -ors, especially plural or agentive noun endings
en.rg_summary: The neuron forms a word-ending branch centered on -ors in later stages, but also undergoes unrelated lexical changes and retains unrelated activations, showing a mixture of recursive generalization and superposition.
en.rg_evidence: Early-to-middle patterns change repeatedly and have little overlap with the final state. After about 32000, coarse rises persistently, and tok is also high from 64000 onward, indicating that the neuron gradually stabilizes and expands around the English word ending -ors in later stages. Unrelated responses such as DIRECTORY remain in the final state.
en.diff_summary: The neuron undergoes clear conceptual drift, converging on the -ors word-ending feature around 64k rather than gradually denoising an initially vague version of the same concept.
en.diff_evidence: Early responses are primarily malformations/formations. From 2k–48k, distinct patterns appear in sequence, including word endings, review, taxonomy, paper formatting, and spectroscopy. Only by 64k does the neuron stably represent the English plural ending -ors, with tok/doc then gradually approaching the final state. Clarity and det fluctuate repeatedly, so this cannot be described as gradual, monotonic denoising.
en.core_summary: Detection of the English plural ending -ors, with especially stable late activation of the ending in subcontractors.

en.diff_evidence: Early triggers include distinct lexical patterns involving difference, CVD, paired/judged, and bound. Steps 6000–64000 then show further drift through related words, substrates, anchoring, and component constraints. Patent mechanical assembly relationships become clearly discernible only at step 96000 and overlap strongly with the final state. Clarity and det fluctuate repeatedly rather than showing monotonically progressive denoising.

en.rg_evidence: The early coefficient pattern disappears after step 256, followed by multiple unrelated word-form or text patterns. The coarse score approaches 1 later on, but tok does not rise to 0.75 until step 128000, and the final interpretation remains scattered. en.diff_evidence: Coefficient dominates early on, followed by distinct patterns including complex, supers, Slavic fragments, Defender, and Canal; the metrics do not show these concepts gradually converging. en.label: U.S. Legal Procedure and Statutory Provisions
en.core: Statutory citations, judicial procedures, and ruling language in U.S. legal texts
en.rg_summary: After initialization and early word-form patterns are replaced, the neuron forms a U.S. legal-text core and gradually generalizes along related branches, including fixed expressions, litigation procedures, and statutory subdivisions.
en.rg_evidence: Early MAT, distance, number, and other patterns and the final tok/doc states are all 0; from step 2000, the neuron enters a legal context, and after step 4000, set collocations and litigation and statutory patterns gradually become more specific. Coarse-grained preference rises from 0.33 at step 2000 to 0.64 at step 4000 and 0.81 at step 6000; after step 96000, tok/doc also approach the final state noticeably. This better fits early training pattern replacement followed by generalization of branches from a legal core, rather than stable monosemy or the coexistence of independent unrelated patterns.
en.diff_summary: The neuron undergoes multiple instances of concept drift early on, shifts to legal texts around step 2000, and only gradually converges to the final statutory and judicial-procedure patterns.
en.diff_evidence: Early patterns shift from MAT and sporadic word forms to distance, stimul, and number, without gradual buildup. Legal concepts become discernible from step 2000, but specific patterns at steps 4000–8000 differ from later statutory and appellate language, and tok and doc fluctuate considerably. Legal-domain preference then gradually stabilizes, while clarity and det still fluctuate, so this does not fit monotonic denoising.
en.core_summary: U.S. legal rulings and litigation texts, with a late-stage stable focus on statutory subdivisions/numbering and their interpretation, also involving grounds for appeal, criminal convictions, and procedural language.
unrelated: MAT letter strings and random word-form patterns at steps 0–128: no quantitative continuity with later legal patterns; considered initialization noise rather than core
Word-form or noun patterns such as distance, stimul, formerly, and number/devices at steps 256–1000: no clear association with one another or with later legal patterns
set phrases coexist with other legal terms at steps 2000–4000, but all belong to the legal-document context; this does not support inferring superposition of unrelated patterns

neurons.rg_evidence: 早期 glob、arthro 等模式没有延续；1000–24000 多次出现清晰但互不相关的词形，符合概念更替或叠加。48000 又短暂形成稳定的 Gutenberg 署名模式，但到 64000 后模式再度分散。末期与最终状态的粗粒度重合上升（coarse 到 0.98），但 tok/doc 不稳定，不能据措辞变化断定有分支链。

step 48000 的 Project Gutenberg 校对团队署名；虽清晰且一致，但与早期词形无可证实关联。
后期（64000–143000）的瑞典语片段、多语种词片段及各类局部词项，彼此关系不明。
neurons.diff_summary: 激活概念多次更替且清晰度非单调，缺乏先粗后细、逐步收敛到最终概念的证据，更符合 drift。
neurons.diff_evidence: 早期 glob 到 128–2000 的 arthro、词内片段及 otherwise/devoid，随后 8000–12000 出现发行销量主题；这些阶段的 tok/doc 几乎为零。48000 突然出现 Gutenberg 署名，之后解释又转为分散的多语词片段；最终 tok/doc=1 仅是定义所致，不能证明渐进去噪。det 与 clarity 多次起落，后期清晰度低。

en.label: Multilingual subword fragments
en.core: none
en.rg_summary: The neuron successively exhibits multiple word-form or corpus patterns with no clear shared core, including a brief stable pattern. Overall, this looks more like a mixture of concept replacement and overlap than recursive generalization.
en.rg_evidence: Early glob and arthro patterns do not persist; from 1000–24000, clear but unrelated word forms appear repeatedly, consistent with concept replacement or overlap. At 48000, a stable Gutenberg credit pattern briefly emerges, but after 64000 the patterns become sporadic again. Coarse overlap with the late and final states increases (coarse to 0.98), but tok/doc is unstable, so wording changes do not establish a branch chain.
en.diff_summary: The activated concepts change repeatedly, and clarity is non-monotonic. There is no evidence of progressing from coarse to fine and gradually converging on a final concept; drift is a better fit.
en.diff_evidence: Early glob is followed by arthro at 128–2000, word-internal fragments, and otherwise/devoid; a release-and-sales theme then appears at 8000–12000. During these stages, tok/doc is nearly zero. Gutenberg credits appear abruptly at 48000, after which explanations shift back to sporadic multilingual subword fragments; the final tok/doc=1 is due only to the definition and does not demonstrate gradual denoising. det and clarity rise and fall repeatedly, and clarity is low in the later stages.
en.core_summary: Early patterns drift repeatedly. The core concept that appears in the middle and persists into later stages is descriptions of releases and sales for works such as music and games, especially copies-based sales expressions. Later triggers generalize toward subword fragments, with reduced stability.
unrelated: The multiple distinct word forms/lexical items at step 1000–24000: otherwise, devoid, burden, copies/release, -able, etc.; no stable shared core or branch chain is apparent among them.
The Project Gutenberg proofreading-team credits at step 48000; although clear and consistent, they have no verifiable connection to the early word forms.
The Swedish fragments, multilingual subword fragments, and various local lexical items in the later period (64000–143000); their relationships are unclear.

en.label: English word-final fragments
en.core: English subword fragments within and at the ends of words; in the middle and later stages, primarily responds to word endings and derivational suffixes rather than stable semantic concepts
en.rg_summary: The neuron shifts among multiple unrelated string patterns early on, then gradually favors fragments within and at the ends of words. Overall, superposition coexists with convergence toward morphological patterns in later stages.
en.rg_evidence: Early Evan and auditory patterns show little overlap across checkpoints. After step 2000, the neuron switches repeatedly to orthographic fragments with no semantic connection, supporting superposition. Later, a more continuous tendency toward word endings and suffixes appears (coarse gradually rises, and tok increases later), but fine-grained document overlap remains weak. This is more consistent with increasingly concentrated morphological triggers than with clear recursive branches.
en.diff_summary: The neuron undergoes several visible pattern shifts and only gradually approaches its final word-form fragment response; this does not fit smooth, monotonic diffusion-style denoising.
en.diff_evidence: Steps 0–256 are mainly Evan/auditory; steps 512–1000 shift to Blues; steps 2000–24000 show ighter, bird, and various within-word fragments. It then gradually favors word-final fragments. Quantitative overlap shows that the final state reaches tok=0.42 only at step 32000, fluctuates at steps 48000–96000, and reaches 0.81 only at 128000. det, clarity, and snr are also non-monotonic, and final clarity=1.
en.core_summary: The earlier stage is triggered by the Evan string; later, there is no stable overarching semantic concept, and responses mainly shift to spelling-sensitive fragments within words and at word endings.

en.label: In-word on/in fragments
en.core: Local in-word letter/subword fragments (ultimately biased toward on, in, and neocon word forms)
en.rg_summary: This neuron underwent multiple unrelated lexical pattern shifts early on, then later trended toward responses to in-word character fragments. Its overall evolution is mixed, rather than a clear recursive generalization chain.
en.rg_evidence: Early AMP disappeared after step 128; from step 256–12000, distinct patterns appeared in sequence: might, word fragments, function, analytic, and others. After step 16000, responses gradually favored in-word substrings; tok rose from 0.66 at step 24000 to 0.97 at step 32000, and coarse approached the final state, but doc remained low until near the end (0.45 at step 96000). Later responses show local spelling continuity, but no clear shared semantic core.
en.diff_summary: The neuron underwent multiple instances of conceptual drift, only stabilizing late on a mixed response involving word-form fragments. This does not fit an evolution from noise through gradual denoising.
en.diff_evidence: Early responses detected AMP characters. At steps 256–512, the pattern shifted to might/possibility; from steps 1000–6000, it shifted through lems, spect/clim, function, and analytic. en.core: Academic markers and citations in scholarly-paper contexts, followed by a preference for astrophysics papers; later shifts to subword fragments in cross-domain technical terms and proper names
en.rg_summary: The neuron first passes through several unstable orthographic patterns, then briefly develops a preference for academic papers and astronomy, and ultimately becomes a detector for cross-domain technical-term fragments without a unified semantic core, reflecting a mixture of replacement and superposition.
en.rg_evidence: Patterns change across steps 0–512 and have little overlap with later patterns. Steps 2000–16000 form an academic-paper/astronomy phase, with coarse rising from 0.34 to 0.70. neurons.label: 代码标识符与语法结构
neurons.core: 代码语境中的标识符与语法结构（后来表现为广泛的代码 token/操作），但没有证据表明最终的日志、方法定义等模式是由早期具体模式递归长出
neurons.rg_summary: 神经元先后经历 Ap、queue、handler 等不同触发模式，之后稳定在宽泛代码领域，却不断更换局部特征，呈现概念替换与代码模式共存，而非清晰的递归分支演化。
neurons.rg_evidence: 早期 Ap 模式及 step 512 的 queue 模式均未延续；step 1000 起转向代码领域，coarse 从此趋近最终状态，tok 到 step 24000–32000 才明显接近。后期共享代码语境，但具体触发模式多变、无可追溯分支链，支持混合的替换与无关模式共存，非明确递归泛化。
unrelated: step 0–256 的 Ap 子串模式：初始化期弱证据，未延续到后期
step 512 的 queue/bottom 词汇模式，与后续代码模式无关
step 1000 的 handler 词模式，随后被更广泛的代码激活取代
step 32000 的 len 操作、step 48000 的 %d 与标点、step 64000 的循环/UI/数据读写等局部模式彼此不构成清晰分支链
最终检查点的日志调用、方法定义、分页界面和数学表达式，缺乏共同核心的明确证据
neurons.diff_summary: 神经元经历了早期字符触发到代码相关偏好的概念漂移，粗粒度偏好先稳定，但整体不符合扩散式渐进去噪。
neurons.diff_evidence: 早期围绕 Ap 子串，step 512 转为 queue，step 1000 起转向代码/handler；这不是逐步收敛到最终概念。粗粒度代码偏好较早稳定，但 tok 到 step 24000 才达 0.67，doc 始终偏低且波动。clarity、det、snr 多次起伏，后期也未持续变清晰。

en.label: Code Identifiers and Syntactic Structures
en.core: Identifiers and syntactic structures in code contexts (later expressed as broad code tokens/operations), but there is no evidence that final patterns such as logs and method definitions recursively grew from specific early patterns
en.rg_summary: The neuron successively exhibited different trigger patterns, including Ap, queue, and handler, then stabilized in the broad code domain while continually changing local features. This indicates concept replacement and code-pattern co-occurrence, rather than clear recursive branch evolution.
en.rg_evidence: The early Ap pattern and the queue pattern at step 512 did not persist. Starting at step 1000, the neuron shifted to the code domain, with coarse approaching its final state from then on; tok did not clearly approach it until step 24000–32000. Later patterns shared a code context, but specific triggers varied and there was no traceable branch chain. This supports a mixture of replacement and unrelated pattern co-occurrence, not explicit recursive generalization.
en.diff_summary: The neuron drifted from early character triggers to code-related preferences. Its coarse-grained preference stabilized first, but overall it does not fit gradual diffusion-style denoising.
en.diff_evidence: Early patterns centered on the Ap substring; at step 512, the neuron shifted to queue, and from step 1000 it shifted to code/handler. This was not gradual convergence toward the final concept. The coarse-grained code preference stabilized relatively early, but tok reached 0.67 only at step 24000, while doc remained low and fluctuating. clarity, det, and snr fluctuated repeatedly, and did not continue to become clearer in the later stages.
en.core_summary: Code structures and identifiers in programming source code; later triggers were spread across syntax, identifiers, length operations, loops, and logs, with no single stable narrow concept.
unrelated: Ap substring pattern at step 0–256: weak evidence in the initialization phase, not sustained later
queue/bottom lexical pattern at step 512, unrelated to subsequent code patterns
handler word pattern at step 1000, subsequently replaced by broader code activation
len operation at step 32000, %d and punctuation at step 48000, and loop/UI/data read-write patterns at step 64000 do not form clear branch chains
Log calls, method definitions, pagination interfaces, and mathematical expressions at the final checkpoint lack clear evidence of a shared core

neurons.rg_evidence: 早期的 Ne、102、Mad、Pars、clim 等模式没有持续成为核心；step 1000 的 clim- 词族也未延续。后期措辞虽多变，但 tok/doc 逐渐接近最终状态，最终仍由链接标记、胆固醇词片段等不同模式构成，未见可追溯的分支链。

neurons.diff_summary: 神经元呈现显著的阶段性概念漂移与后续缓慢重合，而非从模糊粗结构逐步去噪为清晰最终概念。
neurons.diff_evidence: 早期模式从 Ne、数学符号/词形、102、clim 到 normalization、figured 等反复变化；step 12000 前 tok/doc 基本为零，之后也逐步而不稳定地接近最终检查点。det 与 clarity 多次升降，最终解释仍分散且 clarity=2。明显不符合平滑去噪式收敛。

en.label: Heterogeneous intra-word fragments
en.core: none
en.rg_summary: The neuron's early patterns change frequently, then stabilize into the coexistence of multiple unrelated local subword fragments and formatting features, more consistent with superposition.
en.rg_evidence: Early patterns such as Ne, 102, Mad, Pars, and clim do not persist as the core; the clim- family at step 1000 also does not continue. Although the wording varies later, tok/doc gradually approach the final state. The final state still consists of distinct patterns, including link markers and cholesterol subword fragments, with no traceable branch chain.
en.diff_summary: The neuron shows pronounced stage-wise conceptual drift followed by gradual overlap, rather than denoising from a vague coarse structure into a clear final concept.
en.diff_evidence: Early patterns repeatedly shift from Ne, mathematical symbols/word forms, 102, and clim to normalization and figured; tok/doc remain essentially zero before step 12000, then approach the final checkpoint gradually and unstably. det and clarity rise and fall multiple times, and the final interpretation remains dispersed with clarity=2. This clearly does not fit smooth denoising convergence.
en.core_summary: There is no single core concept that remains stable across later checkpoints; later states show a variety of subword fragments, text structures, and formatting features.
unrelated: clim- family at step 1000
normalization and Russian пос- fragment at step 2000
figured at step 4000
code, links, typography, and various medical subword fragments at steps 12000–143000

en.label: Multilingual word-internal fragments
en.core: none
en.rg_summary: This neuron shifted from early growth activation to a long-standing preference for difficult-to-interpret word fragments. Later, it stabilized on multilingual formal text, but lacks a traceable conceptual core.
en.rg_evidence: The early growth pattern had disappeared by step 128; afterward, the neuron primarily showed hard-to-unify word fragments and sporadic patterns for an extended period. Although it gradually shifted toward multilingual formal text later on, with high overlap by step 128000, there is no evidence that this grew from an early core branch; detection scores were also mostly low or unstable.
en.diff_summary: The neuron underwent clear conceptual drift, then gradually converged on word-fragment patterns in multilingual formal text, rather than undergoing smooth denoising from the beginning.
en.diff_evidence: The early growth concept shifted to heterogeneous patterns such as code symbols and word fragments by step 128–2000; it remained unstable at step 4000–12000. The multilingual formal-text/word-fragment pattern gradually emerged only after about step 24000, with tok/doc later rising to 1. det, clarity, and snr fluctuated, showing no monotonic denoising.
en.core_summary: Later, it stably preferred word-internal subword fragments in multilingual formal text, especially iz; this is not a stable semantic theme.

en.diff_summary: The neuron undergoes multiple concept drifts, ultimately settling on a low-clarity intra-word character-fragment pattern rather than gradually denoising and converging from an ambiguous state.

en.label: Device Terms and Compound-Word Fragments
en.core: The cell token and its use for biological cells or basic units
en.rg_summary: The neuron responds briefly to conflict, then develops cell-related patterns, and later shifts to technical terms and compound-word fragments. There is some local generalization, but also substantial replacement by unrelated patterns; overall, this resembles mixed evolution rather than clear recursive generalization.
en.rg_evidence: The cell pattern from step 256–1000 shows local semantic extension, but metrics indicate a marked shift after step 2000: coarse changes from negative to positive, while tok/doc rises only gradually by step 24000. The final interpretation no longer retains the cell core. Although later patterns show broad commonality among compound-word fragments, this is insufficient to establish that they were generated along a cell branch lineage.
en.diff_summary: The neuron undergoes multiple instances of conceptual drift, converging only later on local word-fragment responses. Although there are signs of a coarse-to-fine progression, overall it does not fit smooth, monotonic, diffusion-like evolution.
en.diff_evidence: Early responses repeatedly identify conflict, then shift to cell from step 256 to 1000; at step 2000 they shift again to stem, and activation is scattered from 4000–16000, before gradually converging on compound-word and technical-word fragments. The final matching metrics improve noticeably only much later: coarse is already high at 24000, while tok/doc only gradually approaches its final state after 32000. det, clarity, and snr fluctuate substantially; the final det=0.62、clarity=2, with no monotonic denoising-like increase in clarity.
en.core_summary: Word fragments in English compound words and technical terms, responding mainly in later stages to compound components and suffixes; they do not correspond to a single semantic concept.

en.label: Cross-domain intra-word fragments
en.core: Detection of cross-domain intra-word character/subword fragments
en.rg_summary: The neuron's early pattern is unstable. Later, it develops broad local-string sensitivity and coexists with multiple unrelated trigger patterns, exhibiting superposition along with a weaker preference for shared forms.
en.rg_evidence: The random-initialization phase is not a conceptual core; air/Hart/Cr at steps 0–256 show no persistent overlap with later patterns. In late training, coarse and tok gradually approach their final states, but doc remains low, and explanations repeatedly show cross-domain, unrelated local fragments. Overall, this is consistent with a broad orthographic preference superimposed with multiple independent patterns, rather than a clear branch chain.
en.diff_summary: The neuron responds to character fragments that vary across checkpoints, with no clear evidence of gradual denoising or convergence on a final concept.
en.diff_evidence: Early responses mainly involve character fragments such as air/Cr; mid-training patterns change frequently, and det and clarity fluctuate. In the late stage, tok rises to 0.72, but doc remains at just 0.35, and the final explanation still consists of scattered intra-word fragments. There is no clear evidence of sustained convergence on a final concept.
en.core_summary: Detection of intra-word character and subword fragments; in late training, the neuron stably shows sensitivity to local orthographic fragments across different words, rather than to a fixed semantic concept.
unrelated: Various word fragments and final triggers, including Cr/chemical symbols, angle and technical symbols, over, Pareto/Java/legal fragments, to/phone/other, and, Narrative, lash/IST/ative, blade, Leslie, Polish fragments, email addresses, and code identifiers; there is no evidence that they all derive from a specific early pattern.

en.label: Multilingual subword fragments
en.core: none
en.rg_summary: This neuron shifts from early random word-fragment activations to later cross-lingual local-substring responses, but has no clear, stable core or interpretable recursive branch.
en.rg_evidence: The early NI explanation appears during random initialization and is unrelated to later patterns; Living at step 512 also does not persist. Later explanations are mostly sporadic within-word fragments and names, which look more like hard-to-interpret substring activations than evidence-supported coexistence of distinct semantic patterns. Coarse rises earlier, while tok/doc approach the final state only later, indicating continuing representational change with no traceable branch chain.
en.diff_summary: This neuron does not show a progression from an ambiguous state through denoising to a stable final concept. Instead, it appears to drift several times mid-training and ultimately settle on broad within-word fragment responses.
en.diff_evidence: Early patterns center on NI, shifting to Living at step 512, followed by multiple unstable word-fragment or code patterns; the final checkpoint still consists of scattered within-word subword fragments. tok/doc similarity to the final state rises only later, indicating increasing sample overlap, but interpretability and concepts do not progressively converge.
en.core_summary: In late training, the neuron responds mainly to within-word subwords and local character-form fragments, especially in morphologically complex multilingual words; it has no stable, single semantic concept.

en.label: Multilingual word-form fragments
en.core: Multilingual within-word substrings/subword fragments, later dominated by en and similar word-final fragments
en.rg_summary: The neuron initially shows several unrelated triggers, then shifts to detecting within-word substrings across languages. The evidence favors concept replacement over recursive generalization or stable superposition of co-resident features.
en.rg_evidence: Heterogeneous early triggers such as pers/once and Portland/pragma once lack a common core; from step 512 onward, the neuron gradually shifts to ene/en-like within-word fragments across languages. Coarse remains high for a long time, but tok rises noticeably only at step 6000, so quantitative overlap better supports gradual stabilization of the later pattern than an early core growing a branch.
en.diff_summary: Overall, the pattern evolves gradually, with coarse features converging first and details stabilizing later, but clarity fluctuates substantially and early triggers differ considerably from the final pattern.
en.diff_evidence: Early triggers such as pers, once, and Portland have very little overlap with the final within-word subword fragments. From step 4000 onward, code/morpheme-boundary patterns emerge and then gradually stabilize into within-word fragments across languages. No single semantic concept persists throughout, and early triggers are clearly heterogeneous; however, coarse rises before tok/doc, which is more consistent with coarse-to-fine gradual convergence. det, clarity, and snr fluctuate repeatedly, and clarity does not increase monotonically.
en.core_summary: Within-word subword fragments across languages, especially en letter sequences and adjacent word-final/tokenization fragments; no stable single semantic concept is present later.
unrelated: Character- or word-level triggers such as pers, once, Portland, and pragma once at steps 0–256 do not form a clear branch relationship with the later within-word fragment pattern

en.label: on the contrary and just
en.core: Late local lexical/phrase triggers, mainly the English “on the contrary” and Swedish “just”; no stable semantic core that persists throughout training and gradually develops branches is evident
en.rg_summary: The neuron undergoes early character/substring pattern changes, followed by the coexistence of local expressions such as contrary and just. This is more consistent with heterogeneous pattern coexistence than recursive generalization.
en.rg_evidence: Early patterns change markedly. After step 1000, correlation between the coarse and final states gradually increases, but tok reaches 0.88 only at 96000, while doc is 0.62 at 96000. The late stages show two trigger types, contrary and just, but there is no evidence that they recursively develop from a shared core. Heterogeneous triggers, including multilingual fragments and symbols, also occur in the middle stages, supporting mixed, though the pattern interpretation remains uncertain.
en.diff_summary: The final local lexical patterns stabilize only late, after marked heterogeneous drift and fluctuations in clarity, which is inconsistent with smooth diffusion-like denoising.
en.diff_evidence: Early stages are dominated by character or subword-fragment patterns such as prime, k, and As/O. The As/as pattern at step 1000 has high overlap with the final state (tok=0.88), but steps 2000–24000 show O, subword fragments, and heterogeneous multilingual patterns with low quantitative overlap. Contrast expressions gradually emerge after step 32000; only by 96000, with tok=0.88 and doc=0.62, do they approach the final contrary/just pattern. Clarity rises and falls multiple times, indicating non-monotonic denoising.
en.core_summary: Contrastive and adversative expressions, especially the English phrase “on the contrary”
unrelated: step 0–128: Initialization-stage patterns such as prime numbers and the letter k, with low overlap later; not considered core
step 1000–12000: Character or substring patterns such as As/as, O/o, and O in chemical formulas
step 16000–24000: Heterogeneous patterns such as ro, -ian, function words, and multilingual subword fragments
step 32000–64000: Coexistence of contrary/contrast expressions with other triggers such as fibro-ro and demain
step 96000–143000: English contrary and Swedish just coexist, alongside Lithuanian ir

en.label: Existential there
en.core: there in English existential sentences or at clause onset
en.rg_summary: The neuron's early patterns repeatedly change, later forming a stable existential-there core, but with unrelated number-theory questions and sporadic triggers in between. Overall, this better fits mixed evolution than pure recursive generalization.
en.rg_evidence: Early trigger patterns vary and do not persist; there appears at step 16000, and from step 32000 onward the pattern stabilizes as existential there, with tok from 0.98 at 32000 to 0.97 at 128000, supporting a stable late core. However, there is a clear shift to prime/composite questions at 64000–96000, and unrelated fragments remain in the final checkpoint; overlap between coarse- and fine-grained patterns does not prove these patterns originate from a there branch.
en.diff_summary: The neuron undergoes multiple instances of concept drift. Although it converges on an existential-there pattern at step 32000, significant deviations continue afterward, overall inconsistent with smooth diffusion-style denoising.
en.diff_evidence: Early patterns shift repeatedly among Ros, seemed, and intra-word fragments; tok/doc remain low or fluctuate from step 1000–24000, and only at step 32000 does the pattern clearly shift to existential there (tok 0.98). It then shifts again to prime/composite judgments at step 64000 and returns to there at 96000–128000. Clarity and det decline in the final checkpoint, and the final top samples only partially reflect there.

en.label: “following” introducing subsequent content
en.core: Discourse deixis: anaphoric reference to preceding text (above-mentioned/above-described) and introduction of subsequent text (following)
en.rg_summary: The neuron exhibits early unstable patterns, a preceding-text reference pattern, and a later shift to “following” as an introducer of subsequent content. This shows clear pattern replacement and later coexistence of multiple patterns, rather than a single recursive branch.
en.rg_evidence: Early patterns are sporadic and have little metric overlap with the final state, so they should not be treated as core. A preceding-text reference pattern appears consistently from step 8000 and is almost pure at steps 24000–32000. At step 48000, it shifts to “following,” with tok=0.97, indicating replacement of the main pattern. From steps 64000–143000, both types of discourse deixis coexist, with “following” dominant in the final state.
en.diff_summary: The neuron clearly expresses other features early on, then undergoes concept drift, shifting to the final “following” feature only around step 48000.
en.diff_evidence: Interpretations are clear and stable from step 2000, but identify “today”; at steps 8000–32000, the pattern shifts to anaphoric “above-mentioned,” then changes again to “following” at step 48000. tok rises sharply to 0.97 only at step 48000, indicating that the final concept was introduced midway rather than emerging through gradual denoising and convergence. Clarity is generally high in later steps, but fluctuates.

en.label: Mage and magenta orthographic fragments
en.core: M / Mage orthographic fragments, ultimately stabilizing on the shared agent string in Magento/Mage and magenta
en.rg_summary: This neuron initially exhibits several unrelated trigger patterns, then converges late on a branch of shared orthographic fragments in Mage/Magento and magenta. It is therefore a mixed case, combining early pattern replacement with late recursive generalization.
en.rg_evidence: Early patterns change substantially during training: sales at step 6000 and gestational-age/stem fragments at steps 8000–48000 are unrelated to the final Mage/Magenta pattern. From step 64000 onward, coarse, tok, and doc overlap with the final state rises steadily. After step 96000, Magento and magenta share the agent orthography through the endpoint, showing late recursive generalization; overall, there is also clear replacement of unrelated early patterns.
en.diff_summary: After substantial concept drift, the neuron gradually converges from around step 64000 on the final Magento/Mage and magenta orthographic fragments, rather than undergoing smooth, diffuse denoising.
en.diff_evidence: Early patterns are heterogeneous: at step 6000, the neuron briefly and clearly responds to sales; it then shifts several times to gestational age, within-word fragments, and malignant. At step 32000, it generalizes to M-initial word fragments. Only after around step 48000 does it gradually converge on malign/Magento orthographic fragments, with overlap with the final state rising steadily from step 64000. det and clarity fluctuate repeatedly, inconsistent with monotonic denoising.
en.core_summary: The Magento name and its internal agent/Mage orthographic fragments; these appear consistently late in brand, namespace, and API text, with localized sharing in the color word magenta.

en.label: The letter y and its fragments
en.core: Local in-word strings/subword fragments, later concentrated primarily on the letter y and fragments containing y
en.rg_summary: The neuron exhibits multiple unrelated patterns early on, gradually converging later to stable in-word character fragments (especially fragments containing y). It therefore combines superposition with the evolution of a stable later pattern.
en.rg_evidence: Early square brackets, scientific terminology, and forum markers change repeatedly and cannot be treated as reliable branches of a single core. After about 4000, quantitative overlap gradually increases, reaching 0.86–1.00 for tok 64000–143000. Patterns shift mainly to in-word character fragments, especially y/ys/Dy/Dys. This better fits stable later local-string features accompanied by early unrelated patterns.
en.diff_summary: The neuron undergoes substantial mid-course concept drift. A relatively stable subword-fragment preference emerges only after about step 12000; coarse-grained overlap precedes fine-grained overlap.
en.diff_evidence: Early patterns—including Malta, structured text, combustion/X-ray, Raman, and le fragments—change repeatedly; the comment-username pattern appears only at step 12000. Although the preference is stable thereafter and gradually matches the final local-string/subword-fragment core, it does not converge through continuous denoising from an early concept. det and clarity also fluctuate repeatedly; clarity does not increase consistently after about 12000.
en.core_summary: In-word y/ys strings and subword fragments; later activations are broadly distributed across different languages and word forms and do not correspond to a stable semantic concept.

en.label: Structural boundaries and formatting markers
en.core: Structural boundaries and formatting markers (including punctuation, line breaks/separators, formulas, and document markers)
en.rg_summary: The neuron exhibits multiple unrelated patterns early on, then gradually converges on formatting and structural-boundary features. Overall, this is a mixed pattern in which early superposition coexists with later structural-pattern evolution.
en.rg_evidence: Early patterns vary considerably and overlap little with the final state; the then, punch, so, and cross-lingual fragments at steps 4000–24000 do not resemble branches of formatting markers. After step 64000, coarse and tok gradually rise to 0.97 and 0.84, respectively, and later samples shift toward structural and formatting markers, supporting the emergence of a later core. However, function words and content-bearing examples remain in the final state, and evidence for a recursive chain is limited.
en.diff_summary: The neuron undergoes substantial mid-training conceptual drift and only converges on broad structural markers and local collocations later, inconsistent with smooth diffusion-style denoising evolution.
en.diff_evidence: Early patterns shift from practice/pleading to diverse, unstable triggers such as rap, nem, fine, then, punch, and so; patterns more consistent with the final structural markers do not appear until around step 96000. Coarse-grained overlap rises first, but clarity, det, and selectivity fluctuate substantially; after step 128000, tok approaches its final value while doc remains low.
en.core_summary: In later training, text structural boundaries and formatting markers predominate, including separators, punctuation, parentheses, and formula/citation markers; this pattern remains stable through steps 18–19.
unrelated: Early specialized terms such as practice and pleading (steps 0–64)

Word fragments, function words, and cross-lingual local patterns that change repeatedly from steps 1000–24000 (e.g., nem, fine, then, punch, so, and Bulgarian fragments), with no clear connection to the later formatting-marker core

en.label: Cell culture formulas and sporadic subword fragments
en.core: Cell culture methods and formulas in papers (media, serum, antibiotics, especially streptomycin concentration)
en.rg_summary: The neuron gradually shifts toward cell culture formulas in papers at later stages, but also shows clear unrelated patterns. Overall, this better fits a mixed pattern of multiple coexisting modes than simple recursive generalization.
en.rg_evidence: Quantitative overlap shows a large difference between earlier checkpoints and the final state: by step 32000, tok=.56; at step 48000, it rises to .97. However, doc is only .15, indicating that the corpus/documents are still changing. Cell culture methods recur from step 12000 onward and remain in the final samples; unrelated patterns involving formatting, law, and code are also present and cannot be traced to this core.
en.diff_summary: Metrics indicate that later samples gradually approach the final state, but conceptual and clarity evidence is unstable and does not support a clear denoising-style evolution.
en.diff_evidence: Early McN patterns disappear or change repeatedly from step 256 through 24000, and metrics are low and fluctuate. After step 32000, overlap with the final checkpoint gradually increases, but the patterns described at different checkpoints remain diverse, and clarity does not improve monotonically; final clarity=1. This fits neither continuous denoising nor a clearly identifiable abrupt shift or stable consolidation of a single concept.
en.core_summary: Media formulas in cell culture methods, especially serum, penicillin, and streptomycin, along with their concentration units.

en.label: IN letter sequence
en.core: The IN letter sequence in English words (common in TIN, UNITED, CHIN, etc.), co-occurring later with U.S. court-document contexts
en.rg_summary: The neuron undergoes several unstable early patterns, then stabilizes around triggers for IN/TIN strings that are common in legal documents. It shows some signs of recursive generalization, alongside unrelated patterns, so it is classified as mixed.
en.rg_evidence: Early patterns change frequently and cannot be considered a persistent core. After step 12000, coarse remains around 0.91–0.99, while tok rises from 0.12 to 0.95, supporting stabilization of the later state. IN/TIN recurs across multiple checkpoints and extends to different word forms, though the legal context may be an independent co-occurring pattern.
en.diff_summary: Coarse features approach their final state earlier than fine details, but the concept undergoes substantial drift, and clarity does not show a sustained, diffusion-like increase from denoising.
en.diff_evidence: Early patterns are sporadic. NS appears at step 128, followed by a shift to tildes, legal documents, and Court from step 512 to 8000. After step 12000, legal formatting and IN/TIN character fragments gradually become dominant. Overlap scores indicate representational drift midway through training: tok only clearly approaches its final state at step 32000, while doc remains low through the endpoint. det and clarity fluctuate repeatedly, with no sustained increase in clarity later on.
en.core_summary: Detection of IN/TIN letter sequences within words, especially when embedded in longer English words or proper nouns; this stabilizes later but does not represent a stable semantic concept.
